text:
jonathan: quick heads-up — ran a perf sweep this morning after the kernel-selector tweak and we're seeing a regression for medium-length sequences on a100/h100 when kv cache is fragmented. attaching short profile output below :eyes:

maria: can you paste the exact profiler output? is this across the same model family?

jonathan: pasted, small excerpt: 

```
# perf summary (a100, seq=512, batch token budget=8192)
kernel_select: chosen=triton_v2 (70%), fallback=cuBLAS (30%)
avg_token_latency: 5.2ms -> 6.8ms (regression ~30%)
KV memcpy stalls: 11% -> 28% (after selector change)
packing_utilization: 0.62 -> 0.41
```

jonathan: so main signal is packing_utilization drop + memcpy stalls spike after the selector started preferring triton_v2 for mid seqs. not sure if selector mis-evaluates when kv tensors are fragmented.

kevin: interesting. triton kernels expect contiguous kv layout to hit fast path. if fragmentation forces extra copies we lose. could be our packer not coalescing smaller KV fragments into the batch.

maria: agree. we should try lowering max_tokens_per_batch on a100/h100 for this workload to keep batches denser. current defaults are: a10=4096, t4=2048, l4=1024, a100=12288, h100=16384.

anil: those a100/h100 defaults are aggressive. suggestion: temporarily cap max_tokens_per_batch to reduce fragmentation surface. proposal: a10=4096, t4=2048, l4=1536, a100=8192, h100=12288. also add a kernel_selector threshold to prefer cuBLAS when packing_utilization < 0.5 to avoid extra mem copies.

maria: +1 for selector threshold. but we should be careful not to bias away from triton for very long sequences where triton is better. threshold needs to be conditional on seq distribution, not just a single util metric.

kevin: proof-of-concept change I ran locally: 
```json
{"device_policies": {"A100": {"max_tokens_per_batch": 8192, "kernel_pref": "auto", "packing_util_low_threshold": 0.5}, "H100": {"max_tokens_per_batch": 12288}}}
```

kevin: with that, avg latency on the sampled traces dropped back ~12% relative to the regressed baseline. KV memcpy stalls down to 14%.

jonathan: nice. do we have perf-bot aggregated numbers across a few models?

perf-bot: automated sweep results: 
- model: redwood-7b, traces: 1200 requests
- device: A100 (mixed seqs)
- baseline (old selector + a100=12288): p95_token_latency=13.4ms
- after selector tweak: p95=17.1ms (+27%)
- with cap a100=8192 + packing threshold: p95=15.0ms (-12% from regressed but +11% from baseline)

maria: so cap recovers most regression but not all — expected because we're trading throughput headroom for packing efficiency.

anil: operational idea: add per-GPU token budget weights and a queue policy that prefers smaller batches when packing_util < 0.55. i.e., route requests preferentially to GPUs where they will pack well. that should increase overall utilization without dropping capacity targets.

sara: deployment plan? need canary + rollout gates. also make sure console exposes per-device packing_util metric so SRE can abort if throughput drops too much.

infra-bot: feature-flag 'adaptive-packing-caps' created. canary pool: 20 A100 + 10 H100 nodes. rollover window: 2 hours.

kevin: for experiments let's try two knobs simultaneously: 1) max_tokens_per_batch cap per GPU (as above) 2) kernel_selector packing threshold (0.5) + prefer-cuBLAS-on-low-pack. we should run a 48h canary with traffic split 5%.

maria: also add an experiment that only changes selector (no caps) to isolate which knob is primary cause.

jonathan: agreed. i'll file the experiment ticket and add the config diff. quick config to land in runtime repo (proto):

```yaml
device_policy:
  A100:
    max_tokens_per_batch: 8192
    packing_util_low_threshold: 0.5
    select_pref_on_low_util: cuBLAS
  H100:
    max_tokens_per_batch: 12288
    packing_util_low_threshold: 0.5
    select_pref_on_low_util: cuBLAS
  L4:
    max_tokens_per_batch: 1536
  A10:
    max_tokens_per_batch: 4096
  T4:
    max_tokens_per_batch: 2048
```

jonathan: I'll kick off the canary after PR + perf dashboards. anyone object?

kevin: go ahead. keep an eye on embedding workloads — they have different seq distributions.

maria: one last ask: add a short eval harness that replays saved traces but toggles packing options so we can compare kernel selection decisions deterministically before canary.

jonathan: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:

infra-bot: canary scheduled: start=1719835800, end=1719922200, traffic=5%

jonathan: perfect. follow-ups: @maria to add dashboards, @kevin to open selector-only experiment, @anil to add queue-policy PR.
